decisive_items: Positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies
Complement levels: C3 of 42 mg/dL; C4 of 3 mg/dL (hypocomplementemia)
response.rationale: Systemic lupus erythematosus is the unifying diagnosis given the history, positive anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith antibodies, hypocomplementemia, and biopsy showing interface changes. ACLE is a cutaneous manifestation but does not capture the systemic serologic and hematologic findings. SJS lacks mucosal involvement and drug history; lupus nephritis has no renal evidence.

rejected.why: Represents a skin-limited manifestation of SLE, not the most likely overall diagnosis given systemic serologic and hematologic abnormalities.
No renal findings or evidence of nephritis; anemia and hypocomplementemia are nonspecific and better explained by active SLE.
Atypical targets and blisters are present, but no mucosal involvement or drug trigger; biopsy and serology strongly favor SLE.
